newsitem.title: UK: British regulators to start action against Fidelity.
newsitem.headline: British regulators to start action against Fidelity.

text.p: British financial regulators said Friday they would take action against Fidelity Brokerage Services over problems with customer service that came to light last year.
But the Securities and Futures Authority did not specify what steps it would take against Fidelity, the British retail brokerage arm of the largest mutual fund company in the United States.

Fidelity promised in November to restore "satisfactory" service to clients by January after computer glitches caused accounting and reconciliation problems, and promised compensation to customers who had lost out as a result.

The SFA said in statement that "good progress has been made, but further work is still required before SFA can be confident that Fidelity Brokerage Services is offering a level of customer service which is consistently satisfactory."
It said it would continue to monitor closely Fidelity's customer service performance and would oversee the resolution of outstanding customer complaints and enquiries.

It said it would take into account the speed with which Fidelity resolved outstanding problems "in determining the nature and extent of disciplinary proceedings and the scale of the penalty which is sought."
The watchdog agency also extended to the end of April restrictions on Fidelity, preventing it from taking on new direct customers or introducing new services.
It added that it was satisfied the firm had resources and backing to ensure investors' funds and securities were "not in any jeopardy."
